ga.name: Georgia (statewide)
ga.bounds: Every Georgia migratory bird season is statewide.
ga.note: One zone. WMAs, refuges and some lakes add their own days, hours and distances.

seasonsNote: Every season is statewide. Many WMAs allow waterfowl only on listed days, often ending at noon (amber on the map).

seasons.label: Canada geese — September
seasons.note: No snow or white-fronted geese in September.

seasons.label: Canada geese — regular
seasons.note: White-fronted geese from Oct 10, with Canada geese.

bags.detail: Six ducks, inside which the limits below apply. Possession three times the daily limit (federal rule).
In addition to the other ducks.
Inside the 6: no more than 3 scoters, 3 eiders (1 hen) or 3 long-tailed ducks.
Snow geese 5; white-fronted geese count with Canada geese.
Waterfowl and geese at the regular limits.

duckSublimits.note: no more than 3 scoters, 3 eiders (1 hen), 3 long-tailed ducks

rules.d: One-half hour before sunrise to sunset for all migratory birds. Many WMAs end waterfowl hunting at noon (see each amber area).
10-gauge or smaller with federally approved non-toxic shot of size F or smaller. No lead shot in possession while hunting waterfowl.
No more than 3 shells in the magazine and chamber combined for migratory birds.
No hunting within 600 feet of a dock, house, structure, bridge, road, boat ramp, marina or open recreation area. Contact the Game Management Region office for open dates and rules. Amber on the map.

No hunting within 600 feet of a dock, house, structure, bridge, road, boat ramp, marina or open recreation area on the Georgia side. Waterfowl hunting from land only in the designated “Hunting Areas”. A Corps of Engineers permit is required everywhere on the lake except Eufaula NWR. Amber on the map.

Lakes Burton, Seed, Rabun, Tallulah Falls, Tugalo and Yonah are open for ducks and geese; no hunting within 300 feet of any dock, house, boat ramp, marina or open recreation area without permission. Contact Region 2 (770-535-5700) for dates. Amber on the map.
No hunting within 300 feet of a dock, house, structure, bridge, road, boat ramp, marina or open recreation area (Lake Oliver south of Standing Boy Creek). Amber on the map.

Each WMA lists its own waterfowl days and hours; many are Wednesdays and Saturdays only, end at noon, or are quota hunts. WMAs whose rules differ from the state seasons are amber, with their wording. WRD-designated waterfowl refuges are red.

rules.t: Youth, active-duty military and veterans days
rules.d: Nov 14–15, 2026. Youth under 16 with an adult 18+ who may not hunt. Veterans and active-duty military with their usual licences.
Anyone holding another hunter’s birds needs, in writing, that hunter’s signature, address, number of birds by species and dates taken. Report banded birds at reportband.gov.

licences.d: Required for doves, ducks, geese, woodcock, snipe, coots, rails and gallinules. Free with Sportsman’s, Youth Sportsman’s, disability, honorary and lifetime licences, and for resident landowners on their own land.
Electronic stamp valid July 1 – June 30; landowners included.
